h: Seven Falls Prepare the Final Redemption

p: בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה עח, ח) עַל פָּסוּק: "וַיִּשְׁתַּחוּ אַרְצָה שֶׁבַע פְּעָמִים" (בְּרֵאשִׁית לג, ג):
— In Bereishit Rabbah (78:8) on the verse: "and he bowed himself to the ground seven times" (Genesis 33:3):
לָמָּה שֶׁבַע? עַיֵּין שָׁם: "כִּי שֶׁבַע יִפּוֹל צַדִּיק וָקָם" (מִשְׁלֵי כד, טז).
— Why seven? See there: "For a righteous man falls seven times, and rises up again" (Proverbs 24:16).
לְשׁוֹן "צַדִּיק" יוֹרֶה עַל מִי שֶׁכְּבָר נִשְׁלַם,
— The title "tzaddik" denotes one who has already attained spiritual completion,
וְעִם כָּל זֶה יֵשׁ לוֹ עוֹד נְפִילוֹת.
— and nonetheless he experiences further falls.
וּכְמוֹ יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, לְאַחַר שֶׁכְּבָר נִצַּח אֶת הַמַּלְאָךְ
— And like our father Jacob, peace be upon him, who, after already vanquishing the angel
וְאָמַר לוֹ: "כִּי שָׂרִיתָ עִם אֱלֹהִים וְעִם אֲנָשִׁים וַתּוּכָל" (בְּרֵאשִׁית לב, כט),
— whereupon the angel told him: "for you have striven with God and with men, and have prevailed",
עִם כָּל זֶה הִרְגִּישׁ שֶׁבְּהֶכְרֵחַ לִהְיוֹת עוֹד כַּמָּה נְפִילוֹת לְבָנָיו עַד שֶׁבַע,
— nonetheless sensed that there must yet be further falls for his descendants up to seven,
כְּדֵי לְהִתְבָּרֵר בְּשֶׁבַע הַמִּדּוֹת הַקְּדוֹשׁוֹת,
— in order to be thoroughly refined across all seven holy emotional attributes (Middot),
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יִהְיֶה "וָקָם" – שֶׁיִּהְיֶה תְּקוּמָה לַהַקְּדוּשָּׁה לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד.
— and through this will be realized "and rises up"—an eternal, unshakeable standing for holiness.

Through this very nullification of all seven of his attributes he was saved from Esau, for all harm that comes to a person comes only because of some small dross within him, like the fly that rests only on a wound. … Since Esau held all seven forces of impurity together, Jacob had to cleave to Hashem with all seven attributes together, and the seven bowings allude to this. Therefore, after he parted from Esau, it is written, ‘And Jacob came whole,’ for now he was whole on every side; and this is why the Midrash brings the verse, ‘In six troubles He will deliver you, and in seven no evil shall touch you.’”

h: The Six Exiles and the Seventh Trial

p: וְעַל זֶה מְרַמֵּז הַפָּסוּק: "בְּשֵׁשׁ צָרוֹת יַצִּילֶךָּ וּבְשֶׁבַע לֹא יִגַּע בְּךָ רָע" (אִיּוֹב ה, יט):
— And to this alludes the verse: "In six troubles He shall deliver you, and in seven no evil shall touch you" (Job 5:19):
שֶׁהַשֵּׁשׁ צָרוֹת מְרַמֵּז עַל הַשִּׁשָּׁה גָּלִיּוֹת שֶׁל כְּלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
— for the "six troubles" allude to the six collective exiles of Israel,
שֶׁנֶּחְשְׁבוּ בְּמִדְרַשׁ רַבָּה (נָשֹׂא פָּרָשָׁה י, ב),
— which were enumerated in Midrash Rabbah (Naso 10:2),
וְהֵם: מִצְרַיִם, וְאַשּׁוּר, וְאַרְבַּע גָּלִיּוֹת (בָּבֶל, יָוָן, פָּרַס, וֶאֱדוֹם),
— namely: Egypt, Assyria, and the four primary monarchies (Babylon, Greece, Persia, and Edom),
שֶׁהֵם לְבָרֵר בָּהֶם כָּל הַמִּדּוֹת הַקְּדוֹשׁוֹת.
— which serve to refine and clarify all the holy attributes from their opposite dross.
"וּבְשֶׁבַע לֹא יִגַּע בְּךָ רָע" – מְרַמֵּז עַל מִלְחֶמֶת גּוֹג וּמָגוֹג,
— "And in seven no evil shall touch you"—alludes to the apocalyptic war of Gog and Magog,
שֶׁלֹּא יַסְפִּיק לְהַגִּיעַ הָרַע, שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לוֹ מַפָּלָה מִיָּד,
— wherein evil will not even manage to inflict harm, suffering immediate downfall,
וְיִהְיֶה רַק פַּחַד, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "יוֹשֵׁב בַּשָּׁמַיִם יִשְׂחָק, ה' יִלְעַג לָמוֹ" (תְּהִלִּים ב, ד).
— remaining merely a dread before God's triumph, as it is written: "He that sits in heaven laughs, the Lord has them in derision" (Psalms 2:4).

The deeds of the fathers are a sign for the children, for in the war of Gog and Magog no evil will touch you.”

h: The Nations Oppose the Holy Attributes

p: וְהֵם בָּאִים לְבָרֵר הַמִּדּוֹת הַקְּדוֹשׁוֹת מֵהַהֵיפֶךְ:
— And these exiles come to refine the holy attributes from their counter-forces:
כִּי מִצְרַיִם – "עֶרְוַת הָאָרֶץ" (בְּרֵאשִׁית מב, ט) –
— For Egypt—"the nakedness of the land"—
הוּא הַמְּנַגֵּד לִבְחִינַת אַהֲבָה וָחֶסֶד שֶׁבִּקְדוּשָּׁה, מִדַּת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
— is the demonic opposite of the attribute of holy Love and Chesed, the trait of Abraham our father, peace be upon him,
וְנֶגֶד זֶה בְּחִינַת הַתַּאֲוָה, קְלִיפַּת יִשְׁמָעֵאל.
— counterbalanced by base lust, the husk of Ishmael.
וְעַל יְדֵי גָּלוּת מִצְרַיִם, שֶׁהָיוּ שְׁטוּפִים בִּזְנוּת, וְיִשְׂרָאֵל גָּדְרוּ אֶת עַצְמָם מֵהָעֶרְוָה,
— And through the Egyptian exile, where the Egyptians were immersed in depravity while Israel fenced themselves in chastity,
זָכוּ לְבָרֵר בְּחִינַת חֶסֶד שֶׁבִּקְדוּשָּׁה.
— they merited to refine the attribute of Chesed in holiness.
וְלָכֵן נֶאֱמַר לְאַבְרָהָם מְפוֹרָשׁ גָּלוּת מִצְרַיִם: "וַעֲבָדוּם וְעִנּוּ אֹתָם" (שָׁם טו, יג),
— Therefore the Egyptian exile was explicitly proclaimed to Abraham: "and shall serve them, and they shall afflict them",
כְּדֵי לְבָרֵר מִדָּתוֹ.
— specifically to clarify his attribute.
וְאִיתָא (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה טז, ד):
— And it is taught (Bereishit Rabbah 16:4):
כָּל הָאוּמּוֹת נִקְרְאוּ עַל שֵׁם מִצְרַיִם, עַל שֵׁם שֶׁהֵם מְצִירוֹת לְיִשְׂרָאֵל;
— all oppressive empires are termed "Egypt" (Mitzrayim), because they distress (meitzirin) Israel;
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁבְּעִנְיָן הַזֶּה יֵשׁ לְכָל נֶפֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל מֵצַר וְדַחַק שֶׁמֵּעִיק לוֹ כְּשֶׁרוֹצֶה לִפְנוֹת אֶת עַצְמוֹ לַהַקְּדוּשָּׁה.
— meaning that in this realm every Jewish soul experiences narrow distress (meitzar) that oppresses him when seeking to turn to holiness.

p: וְאַשּׁוּר – הוּא הַמְּנַגֵּד לְמִדַּת יִצְחָק, הַגְּבוּרָה שֶׁבִּקְדוּשָּׁה,
— And Assyria—is the opposite of Isaac's attribute, holy Gevurah (Might),
וּכְשֵׁם "אַשּׁוּר" שֶׁהוּא לְשׁוֹן תֹּקֶף וְכֹחַ.
— matching the name Ashur, which signifies sheer strength and dominion.
וְכֵן כָּתוּב בְּדִבְרֵי רַבְשָׁקֵה: "עֵצָה וּגְבוּרָה לַמִּלְחָמָה" (יְשַׁעְיָה לו, ה),
— And so Rabshakeh boasted: "counsel and strength for the war",
שֶׁזֶּהוּ תַּכְלִית כֹּחוֹ בַּהַהֵיפֶךְ.
— which is the ultimate exertion of his power in unholiness.
וְגַם כָּל הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת נִקְרְאוּ עַל שֵׁם אַשּׁוּר,
— And all the idolatrous nations are likewise designated after Assyria,
שֶׁהָיוּ מְאַשְּׁרִין עַצְמָן מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמִדְרַשׁ רַבָּה (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה יג, ה).
— for they gloried over Israel (Vayikra Rabbah 13:5).
כִּי אֵלּוּ הַשְּׁתֵּי מִדּוֹת בַּהֵיפֶךְ
— For these two root-traits in the realm of evil
הֵם כְּנֶגֶד קְלִיפּוֹת יִשְׁמָעֵאל וְעֵשָׂו, שֶׁהֵם כְּלָלִיּוּת שֶׁל הַקְּלִיפּוֹת כַּיָּדוּעַ.
— correspond to the primary archetypes of Ishmael (unholy Chesed) and Esau (unholy Gevurah), which encompass all Kelippot as is known.

h: Babylon and Greece Oppose Torah Holiness

p: וּבָבֶל וְיָוָן הֵמָּה הַמְּנַגְּדִים לִקְדוּשַּׁת מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן (נֵצַח וָהוֹד),
— And Babylon and Greece are the adversaries opposing the holiness of Moses and Aaron (Netzach and Hod),
הַיְינוּ לִבְחִינַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה:
— namely the archetypes of the Written Torah and the Oral Torah:
כִּי בָּבֶל מְנַגֵּד לְתוֹרַת מֹשֶׁה,
— For Babylon opposed the Torah of Moses,
שֶׁאָז בְּגָלוּת בָּבֶל הָיָה עוֹד הִתְגַּלּוּת נְבִיאִים שֶׁנִּתְּנוּ לִכְתּוֹב כְּדָנִיֵּאל וַחֲבֵירָיו;
— since during the Babylonian exile prophetic revelation destined for the written canon still functioned, through Daniel and his companions;
וּלְעוּמַּת זֶה הָיָה בַּקְּלִיפָּה בְּכֹחַ זֶה חַרְטֻמִּים וְאַשָּׁפִים וְחַכְמֵי בָבֶל,
— and counter to this in the Kelippah stood magicians, enchanters, and Babylonian astrologers,
וְגַם נֶאֱמַר בָּהֶם: "וּלְלַמְּדָם סֵפֶר וּלְשׁוֹן כַּשְׂדִּים" (דָּנִיֵּאל א, ד),
— and concerning them Scripture says: "and whom they might teach the learning and the tongue of the Chaldeans",
וְהָיָה אָז גַּם יִצְרָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.
— and at that time the impulse for idolatry still raged.

p: אָמְנָם קְלִיפַּת יָוָן הוּא לְנֶגֶד תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, שֶׁהוּא מִדַּת אַהֲרֹן,
— However, the husk of Greece stood counter to the Oral Torah, which is the attribute of Aaron,
דִּכְתִיב: "תּוֹרַת אֱמֶת הָיְתָה בְּפִיהוּ וְגוֹמֵר, כִּי שִׂפְתֵי כֹהֵן יִשְׁמְרוּ דַעַת וְתוֹרָה יְבַקְשׁוּ מִפִּיהוּ" (מַלְאָכִי ב, ו–ז),
— as it is written: "The law of truth was in his mouth... for the priest's lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth",
וְנֶאֱמַר: "וְהָיָה הוּא יִהְיֶה לְּךָ לְפֶה וְגוֹמֵר" (שְׁמוֹת ד, טז);
— and as Hashem told Moses regarding Aaron: "and he shall be your spokesman unto the people, and he shall be to you a mouth";
כִּי אָז בִּימֵי שִׁמְעוֹן הַצַּדִּיק, לְאַחַר שֶׁפָּסְקוּ כְּבָר הִתְגַּלּוּת נְבִיאִים,
— for during the era of Simon the Just, after prophetic revelation had already ceased,
וְהָיָה זְמַן אַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה שֶׁבִּיטְּלוּ יִצְרָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
— and during the era of the Men of the Great Assembly who abolished the impulse for idolatry (Yoma 69b)
וְגָזְרוּ גְּזֵירוֹת לַעֲשׂוֹת סְיָיג לַתּוֹרָה,
— and instituted fences to safeguard the Torah,
וְאָז נֶגֶד זֶה הָיְתָה חָכְמַת יָוָן וְהַצְּדוֹקִים,
— at that time, counterposed against them, arose secular Greek philosophy and the Sadducees,
וְאָז נִתְבָּרֵר קְדוּשַׁת חָכְמַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה עַל יְדֵי הַתַּנָּאִים.
— and through the Tannaim the sanctity of the Oral Torah was purified and firmly established.

h: Persia and Edom Oppose Jacob and Joseph

p: וּפָרַס וֶאֱדוֹם הֵמָּה מְנַגְּדִים לִבְחִינַת יַעֲקֹב וְיוֹסֵף (תִּפְאֶרֶת וִיסוֹד):
— And Persia and Edom are the adversaries opposing Jacob and Joseph (Tiferet and Yesod):
כִּדְאִיתָא (פְּסִיקְתָּא לְפָרָשַׁת פָּרָה יד):
— as taught in the Pesikta (Parashat Parah 14):
"'תְּמִימָה' – זוֹ פָּרַס; וּמָדַי תְּמִימִים הָיוּ? אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: עֲלֵיהֶם אֵין לִי אֶלָּא שֶׁעָבְדוּ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁקִּבְּלוּ מֵאֲבוֹתֵיהֶם בִּלְבַד".

— "'Whole (temimah)'—this is Persia; and were the Medes and Persians wholehearted? The Holy One said: Regarding them, I hold against them only that they practiced idolatry inherited from their ancestors."
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁעַל הַגָּוֶון יֵשׁ לָהֶם תְּמִימוּת מִמִּדַּת יַעֲקֹב "אִישׁ תָּם" (בְּרֵאשִׁית כה, כז);
— Meaning that outwardly they exhibited a counterfeit wholeness mirroring Jacob, "a wholehearted man" (ish tam);
וּכְעֵין שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת ח עַמּוּד ב): "בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה דְבָרִים אוֹהֵב אֲנִי אֶת הַפַּרְסִיִּים וְכוּלֵי, וּצְנוּעִין בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ";
— similar to what is said in Berakhot (8b): "In three things I love the Persians... and they are modest in marital intimacy";
וְאַחַר זֶה אָמַר: "'אֲנִי צִוֵּיתִי לִמְקֻדָּשָׁי' (יְשַׁעְיָה יג, ג) – אֵלּוּ הַפַּרְסִיִּים הַמְקוּדָּשִׁים וּמְזוּמָּנִים לְגֵיהִנָּם".
— yet immediately following it states: "'I have commanded My consecrated ones'—these are the Persians who are consecrated and designated for Gehenna."
וְהַיְינוּ הֲגַם שֶׁעַל הַגָּוֶון נִרְאֶה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם מִדַּת צְנִיעוּת אֲשֶׁר יִשְׂרָאֵל נִקְרְאוּ קְדוֹשִׁים בִּשְׁבִיל זֶה,
— For although outwardly they appear modest—the trait for which Israel is designated holy—
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (מְגִילָּה יג עַמּוּד א) עַל אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ: "מִגְּנוּתוֹ לָמַדְתָּ שִׁבְחוֹ וְכוּלֵי, שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה וְכוּלֵי",
— as expounded in Megillah (13a) regarding Ahasuerus: "from his disparagement you learn his modesty, that he did not have sexual relations during the day,"
וְעַל דָּבָר זֶה אָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת פו עַמּוּד א): "יִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים וְכוּלֵי";
— concerning which it was said in Shabbat (86a): "Israel are holy, etc.";
וְעִם כָּל זֶה הֵם עַל יְדֵי זֶה מְקוּדָּשִׁים וּמְזוּמָּנִים לְגֵיהִנָּם, שֶׁהַצְּנִיעוּת שֶׁלָּהֶם אֵינוֹ מִגֶּדֶר הַקְּדוּשָּׁה.
— nonetheless they are designated for Gehenna, because their modesty did not emerge from holy fear of God.

footnotes.heAnchorPrefix: וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (מְגִילָּה יג עַמּוּד א) עַל אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ: "מִגְּנוּתוֹ לָמַדְתָּ שִׁבְחוֹ וְכוּלֵי, שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה וְכוּלֵי",

paragraphs.text: Megillah 13a: “The verse states: ‘In the evening she went, and in the morning she returned’ (Esther 2:14). Rabbi Yoḥanan said: From the implicit criticism of that wicked man, Ahasuerus, who cohabited with many women, we have incidentally learned his praise as well, that he would not engage in sexual relations during the day, but in a more modest fashion at night.”

paragraphs.text: Shabbat 86a: “The Gemara asks: Why did he need to tell them to separate during the morning hours? Didn’t Rav Huna say: The Jewish people are holy and do not have relations during the day? It was not necessary to command them until night. The Gemara replies: It was necessary to tell them in the morning, as Rava said: If it was a dark house, it is permitted to have relations during the day. And similarly, Rava said, and some say that Rav Pappa said: A Torah scholar obscures the light in the room with his cloak and is thereby permitted to have relations during the day. Therefore, it was necessary to command the people to separate even during the daytime hours.”

p: וֶאֱדוֹם – כְּנֶגֶד בְּחִינַת קְדוּשַׁת יוֹסֵף,
— And Edom—stands counter to the holiness of Joseph,
כִּי אֵין עֲמָלֵק נוֹפֵל אֶלָּא בְּיַד בָּנֶיהָ שֶׁל רָחֵל,
— for Amalek and Edom fall only into the hands of the descendants of Rachel,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַיְהִי כַּאֲשֶׁר יָלְדָה רָחֵל אֶת יוֹסֵף וְגוֹמֵר" (בְּרֵאשִׁית ל, כה),
— as it is written: "And it came to pass, when Rachel had borne Joseph, that Jacob said: Send me away",
שֶׁכְּבָר נוֹלַד שִׂטְנוֹ שֶׁל עֵשָׂו, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (עג, ז).
— for the cosmic adversary of Esau had now been born (Bereishit Rabbah 73:7).

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 73:7: “‘It was when Rachel bore Joseph, Jacob said to Laban: Release me, and I will go to my place and to my land’ (Genesis 30:25). ‘It was when Rachel bore Joseph’ – when Joseph was born, Esau’s adversary was born, as it is stated: ‘Jacob said to Laban: Release me, and I will go to my place and to my land,’ as Rabbi Pinḥas said in the name of Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥman: It is a tradition that Esau will fall only into the hand of the descendants of Rachel. That is what is written: ‘Will the young of the flock not drag them?’ (Jeremiah 49:20) – why does it call them ‘the young of the flock’? It is because they were the youngest of the tribes.”

h: Final Refinement through Gog and Magog

p: וְגוֹג וּמָגוֹג – יִהְיֶה תַּכְלִית הַבֵּירוּר שֶׁל מְשִׁיחַ בֶּן דָּוִד (מַלְכוּת),
— And the war of Gog and Magog—will be the final, ultimate clarification wrought by Mashiach ben David (Malchut),
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "עַל ה' וְעַל מְשִׁיחוֹ" (תְּהִלִּים ב, ב);
— as it is stated: "against Hashem, and against His anointed (Mashiach)" (Psalms 2:2);
וּבְתַכְלִית הַבֵּירוּר הַשְּׁבִיעִי יִהְיֶה הַגְּאוּלָּה הַשְּׁלֵימָה.
— and with the completion of this seventh clarification will dawn the full and final redemption.
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "וַיִּשְׁתַּחוּ אַרְצָה שֶׁבַע פְּעָמִים עַד גִּשְׁתּוֹ עַד אָחִיו" (בְּרֵאשִׁית לג, ג) –
— And concerning this Scripture records: "and he bowed himself to the ground seven times, until he came near to his brother"—
הַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בָּזֶה תַּכְלִית הַקִּימָה,
— meaning that through these seven bowings would emerge the ultimate standing and rising,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְעָלוּ מוֹשִׁעִים בְּהַר צִיּוֹן לִשְׁפֹּט אֶת הַר עֵשָׂו וְהָיְתָה לַה' הַמְּלוּכָה" (עֹבַדְיָה א, כא):
— as it is stated: "And saviors shall come up on Mount Zion to judge the mount of Esau, and the kingdom shall be Hashem's":
